title: Reflect the canonical finite projection/base-change diamond
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a coefficient datum C with prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and an integer n >= 1. Let S be the six-functor datum of [def-sf-datum] at these coefficients, Q a compactified Cartesian square of its finite-type spaces, K a bounded constructible finite-coefficient object on X, and L a bounded constructible finite-coefficient object of finite Tor amplitude on Y. The two ordered routes LeftPath and RightPath of [def-sf-finite-base-change-realization-paths] are equal. No separatedness of the horizontal map is required.

source.place: Base-change paragraph: the canonical proper/open square in the specified operation coordinates

proof.text: The separate realization equations of [lem-sf-finite-base-change-route-realization] identify the inclusion image of each route, followed by the same explicit target isomorphism, with the realized corresponding fixed-scalar diamond route.

The canonical diamond equality from [lem-sf-finite-projection-exchange-transposes] identifies those fixed-scalar routes. Apply the realization functor to this equality, compose with the source comparison, combine with the two coordinate equations, cancel the target isomorphism and reflect equality through the faithful full inclusion.

proof_origin.place: Base-change paragraph: faithful reflection of the realized proper/open square
